title: Founded Amazon in 1994 as an online bookstore
statement: Founded Amazon in 1994, leaving a Wall Street position at D.E. Shaw to build an online bookstore that could offer millions of titles impossible to stock in a physical store.
outcome: Amazon's 1997 letter to shareholders reported 1.5 million customers, 838% revenue growth to $147.8 million, and what Bezos called an enduring franchise in the making.

title: Wrote the 1997 long-term shareholder letter as Amazon's operating constitution
statement: Used Amazon's first letter to shareholders as a public charter, prioritizing long-term market leadership over short-term profitability and committing to choose cash flows over GAAP appearance when the two conflicted.
outcome: The 1997 letter was reprinted and appended to every subsequent annual shareholder letter, anchoring two decades of decisions to take cash flows over reported earnings.

title: Launched Amazon Prime in February 2005
statement: Launched Amazon Prime on February 2, 2005, as a $79-per-year membership offering free two-day shipping on eligible purchases, reframing shipping as a loyalty program rather than a per-transaction fee.
outcome: Prime became the central flywheel of Amazon's retail business, later absorbing video streaming, music, grocery delivery, and pharmacy benefits, and locking in repeat purchase behavior at scale.

title: Launched Amazon Web Services in 2006
statement: Launched Amazon Web Services in the spring of 2006 with Amazon S3 in March and Amazon EC2 in August, turning internal retail infrastructure into a pay-as-you-go utility accessible to anyone.
outcome: AWS became Amazon's highest-margin business and reshaped the global IT infrastructure market, making cloud a foundational utility for the modern internet.

title: Acquired the Washington Post in 2013 through Nash Holdings
statement: Acquired the Washington Post newspaper on August 5, 2013, through a personal holding company called Nash Holdings LLC for $250 million in cash, structuring the deal outside Amazon to preserve editorial independence.
outcome: The purchase excluded the Post Co.'s other media and real estate assets, and gave Bezos personal ownership of a major national newspaper as the industry faced steep pressure on print advertising.

title: Stepped down as Amazon CEO on July 5, 2021
statement: Stepped down as Amazon's chief executive on July 5, 2021, transitioning to executive chairman and handing the CEO role to AWS chief Andy Jassy.
outcome: The transition ended Bezos's 27-year run as CEO and shifted his focus to new products and early initiatives, while preserving his chairmanship of the board.
